item.title: Controlling The Skips of Arithmetic Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.14399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Andrews, Ganchev, Kuyper, Lempp, Miller, A.\ Soskova, and M.\ Soskova conjectured that skip-cototality coincides with weak cototality. We show that the conjecture is false by constructing a $\Pi^0_2$ set whose skip does not have a cototal degree. We further adapt this construction to obtain additional results. We prove that for each odd $n$, there is a $\Pi^0_{n+1}$ degree whose $n$-iterated skip does not have a cototal degree. We show that there is a $\Pi^0_2$ degree which does not contain an introenumerable set.
item.dc:creator: Taeyoung Em

item.title: A Nullstellensatz for the field of complex Laurent series
item.description: arXiv:2610.14417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T$ be the theory of the valued field of complex Laurent series $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$ in the language of rings expanded by a constant for $t$ and by predicates for $n$-th powers. We introduce a $t$-adic analogue of Kochen's operator, namely $\gamma(x)=x/(1+tx^{2})$, and the associated Kochen ring $\Lambda_{L}$ of a field extension $L$ of a model $K$ of $T$. Our main result characterizes the field extensions of $K$ which embed into a model of $T$ (the formally $T$-adic} fields): $L$ is formally $T$-adic if and only if $1/t\notin\Lambda_{L}$. As an application we prove a Nullstellensatz for $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$: a polynomial $f\in K[X_{1},\dots,X_{n}]$ vanishes on the zero set of an ideal $I$ if and only if $f^{m}=\sum_{i}\omega_{i}f_{i}$ for some $m\geqslant 1$, generators $f_{i}$ of $I$ and coefficients $\omega_{i}$ in the ring $\Lambda_{K(X)}\cdot K[X]$. We derive the resulting correspondence between $R$-ideals and algebraic sets, and we compare natural incarnations of the associated $T$-spectrum: prime ideals, morphisms into models of $T$, and the space of types of $T$.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Cubides Kovacsics, Sebasti\'an Uribe Rinc\'on

item.title: Order-preserving maps of the Turing degrees: regularity and consistency strength
item.description: arXiv:2610.14548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a proof of Part~I of Martin's conjecture for order-preserving maps directly on the quotient of the reals by Turing equivalence. The assumptions are countable choice for reals, the perfect-set property for sets of reals, and continuous uniformization on a comeager domain. The argument applies under $\mathsf{AD}+\mathsf{DC}_{\R}$ and inside the choiceless Solovay model. We then determine the exact consistency strength of the unrestricted order-preserving dichotomy as an axiom over $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{AC}_{\omega}(\R)$: it is equiconsistent with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ plus a strongly inaccessible cardinal.
item.dc:creator: Liang Yu

item.title: A Countable Three-Generated Orthomodular Lattice with No $\sigma$-Complete Embedding
item.description: arXiv:2610.14859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an explicit countably infinite orthomodular lattice generated by three specified elements and a direct argument that it admits no injective homomorphism into any $\sigma$-complete orthomodular lattice. In particular, it does not embed into any set-sized complete orthomodular lattice. The source is a generated subalgebra of a cofinite reduced product of finite-dimensional real subspace lattices. A nonzero finite term $a$ is orthogonal to the orbit of a terminal line under every finite word in three Sasaki projections, while another finite term $X$ satisfies $\pi_a\pi_X(t)=a$. If the image of this countable orbit has a supremum in a target orthomodular lattice, Sasaki adjunction forces that supremum to commute with the generator images. This forces the image of $a$ to vanish. The proof imposes no atomicity, modularity, Hilbert representation, cardinality bound on the target, or preservation of source infinitary operations. All target lemmas are derived from the orthomodular axioms.
item.dc:creator: Joaquim Reizi Higuchi (Graduate School, Program in Natural Sciences, The Open University of Japan, Chiba, Japan)

item.title: Nonstandard combinatorial ultrafilters and a new local witness model
item.description: arXiv:2610.15018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central object in the theory of proof complexity generators is Krajicek's local witness model. We construct a new such model as a definable ultrapower using a definable version of a selective ultrafilter over a model of arithmetic. We transfer some set theory of combinatorial ultrafilters to the definable nonstandard setting.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Heil, Moritz M\"uller

item.title: Internal Languages for Thin Epsilon-Hyperdoctrines: Soundness, Completeness, and Rocq Formalization
item.description: arXiv:2610.15080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a typed proof-term calculus for intuitionistic intensional first-order logic with Hilbert's epsilon-operator and prove its soundness and completeness with respect to hyperdoctrinal models with thin bicartesian closed setoid categories (BiCCCs) as fibres and formula-indexed witness selections. The calculus provides an explicit internal language for these epsilon-hyperdoctrines: for each fixed typed signature, its syntactic term model is initial for syntax-indexed, interpretation-preserving model morphisms, with uniqueness up to setoid equality. The nested epsilon syntax is organized by a well-founded dependency relation on formula labels. Concrete countermodels exhibit failure of excluded middle and show that formula conversion need not identify the selected witnesses. We also compare the full calculus with its epsilon-free and epsilon-only fragments. The principal constructions and metatheorems are formalized in Rocq. With setoid BiCCCs, proof irrelevance is a choice of equality, not the erasure of proofs: the proofs and their categorical operations remain available as the basis for a future proof-relevant categorical semantics.
item.dc:creator: Zolt\'an G\'abor Moln\'ar, Csaba T\'oth

item.title: A counterexample to Vaught's Conjecture for $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a sentence of $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$ having exactly $\aleph_1$ many countable models up to isomorphism, but no perfect set of non-isomorphic models. This disproves Vaught's conjecture for infinitary logic. The construction follows a framework devised by Robin Knight, and the proof has been formally verified in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Nathanael L. Ackerman, Cameron E. Freer, Robin W. Knight

item.title: Teams, Truthmakers, Translations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a faithful translation from Aloni's logic BSL into a classical modal logic over semilattices combining ideas from earlier modal translations of truthmaker semantics with algebraic representation theory. We show how our method can also be made to work for other current hyperintensional logics. Finally, we place our results in a broader setting of translating hyperintensional logics into classical modal ones, and discuss applications and new challenges that arise for both areas of philosophical logic connected in this way.
item.dc:creator: Maria Aloni, Alexandru Baltag, Johan van Benthem, Nick Bezhanishvili, S{\o}ren Brinck Knudstorp

item.title: Baire measurable functions and automorphisms of the truth-table degrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.16059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if an automorphism $\pi$ of the truth-table degrees is induced by a Baire measurable function $F\colon 2^{\omega}\to 2^{\omega}$, or merely induced on some comeager set by a continuous function, then $\pi$ is the identity. The same results hold for the weak truth-table degrees. The argument is an adaptation to truth-table reducibility of OpenAI's recent proof that the Turing degrees are rigid.
item.dc:creator: Bj{\o}rn Kjos-Hanssen

item.title: A characterization of the finite model property for $\omega$-categorical theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.16163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A first-order theory $T$ has the {\em finite model property} if every first-order sentence that is implied by $T$ has a finite model. We give a characterization of when a complete $\omega$-categorical theory $T$ has the finite model property. The characterization makes it possible to transfer stability theoretic results in [29] to certain classes of finite structures. This approach also gives information concerning properties that a sequence of finite ``base structures'' of ever larger size must have in order for its random expansions to a larger vocabulary to have a chance to satisfy a convergence law for first-order logic.
item.dc:creator: Vera Koponen

item.title: Remarks on ultrafilters exponentiation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, two exponentiations of ultrafilters have been introduced in [7]. We rephrase them in nonstandard terms, and use the nonstandard formulations to characterize some of their properties. We also study their relations with divisibility by introducing factor-picking functions and highly exponential ultrafilters.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Luperi Baglini, Boris \v{S}obot

item.title: Tight $\sigma$-filtrations and the BFPP of $C(\omega^*)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming that $\mathcal{P}(\omega)$ is tightly $\sigma$-filtered, we prove that $C(\omega^*)$ fails the ball fixed point property. This axiom holds under the continuum hypothesis and in the $\aleph_2$-Cohen model. The proof shows that the Stone space of the countable--cocountable algebra $\operatorname{Cc}(\omega_1)$ is a continuous retract of $\omega^*$ and uses the equivalence between tight $\sigma$-filteredness of $\operatorname{Cc}(\omega_1)$ and of $\mathcal{P}(\omega)$. We also prove that the quotient of a tightly $\sigma$-filtered Boolean algebra $B$ with the countable separation property by an $\aleph_1$-generated $P$-ideal is a Boolean retract of $B$.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Avil\'es, Maur\'icio Rossetto

item.title: Proper varieties of distributive l-pregroups are periodic
item.description: arXiv:2610.16775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every proper variety of distributive $\ell$-pregroups is periodic; as a result, the subvariety lattice of the variety of distributive $\ell$-pregroups decomposes into a disjoint union of bounded intervals each consisting of all properly $n$-periodic varieties, for different $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. On the way, we study non-periodic (one-generated) subalgebras of $\mathbf{F}(\mathbb{Z})$ and show that they either contain a non-periodic idempotent or they contain idempotents of arbitrary big periodicity. The same results holds for non-periodic one-generated subalgebras of $\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{J} \overrightarrow{\times} \mathbb{Z})$, where $\mathbf{J}$ is a chain, generated by a composite element and the resulting idempotents can be taken to be local in the associated wreath product.
item.dc:creator: Nikolaos Galatos, Simon Santschi

item.title: Linear Logic via algebra I: Girard algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.16804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we develop several aspects of the algebraic theory of Girard algebras, regarded as the equivalent algebraic semantics of multiplicative additive Linear Logic $\mathsf{MALL}$. The main structural results concern the bottom of the subvariety lattice of the variety of Girard algebras: varieties generated by simple Girard algebras generated by the constants correspond exactly to the atoms of the lattice. Moreover the lattice itself is atomic, i.e. every nontrivial subvariety contains an atom. These atoms can be represented uniformly by the maximal filters of the free algebra generated by the constants. Moreover every congruence of this free algebra is realized by a subvariety, and the resulting atom-support topology records the behavior of arbitrary joins: the atoms below a join of atoms are precisely the points in the closure of the corresponding subset of the spectrum. The concrete constructions show that the bottom of the lattice is already quite rich. Besides determining the integral and degenerate boundary cases and exhibiting finite modular and nonmodular atoms and chains of covers, we constructed infinite families of atoms whose topology reflects genuinely infinitary behavior; thus finite and infinite joins behave essentially differently at the bottom of the subvariety lattice. On the logical side, these results yield $2^{\aleph_0}$ Post-complete extensions of $\mathsf{MALL}$.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Agliano, Mitar Nedeljkovic

item.title: On the foundations of logic and probability, II. Modal probability spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A class of models which brings to the fore the inner logic of the calculus of probability instead of assigning probabilities to sentences is introduced and investigated.
item.dc:creator: Loic Cosyns

item.title: Functional Projection and Complexity Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.17455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: T\"ornquist (arXiv:1310.3250) proved that if there exists a $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_2$ maximal almost disjoint (MAD) family, then there exists a $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$ MAD family. Since then, several other "complexity reduction" proofs have been found for other combinatorial objects, such as maximal independent families or ultrafilters. All of these proofs have relied on $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$-uniformization, so they did not easily lift to higher projective levels. In this paper, we introduce a principle weaker than Uniformization which we call "Functional Projection", and show that this principle is sufficient for most complexity reduction proofs. On the other hand, we prove that in $L[U]$, the canonical inner model for a measurable cardinal, Functional Projection holds for $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_2$ relations. As an immediate corollary, we obtain that in $L[U]$ there are $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_2$ witnesses for many combinatorial families.
item.dc:creator: Vera Fischer, Yurii Khomskii, Yipu Li, Julia Millhouse

item.title: Fragments of SRP, the nonstationary ideal, and diagonal reflection
item.description: arXiv:2610.17547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the relationships between fragments of SRP and diagonal reflection principles. It turns out that the subcomplete fragment of SRP, augmented with CH, implies that the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$ is not saturated, but that Larson's diagonal reflection principle $OSR_{\omega_2}$ holds. In contrast, it was known that the full principle SRP implies the saturation of the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$, but it does not imply $OSR_{\omega_2}$. We find several instances of this phenomenon: pairing (variations of) the subcomplete fragment of SRP with stronger failures of the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$ to be saturated allows us to conclude more instances of diagonal reflection principles, while boosting (the corresponding variations of) the full principle SRP with strong forms of the saturation of the nonstationary ideal allows us to produce models where these principles still hold, yet weaker versions of diagonal reflection fail.
item.dc:creator: Gunter Fuchs, Hiroshi Sakai

item.title: On separable pairs of fields and beautiful pairs of separably closed valued fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.18753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue the study of beautiful pairs of henselian valued fields, initiated in joint work of the second author with Cubides Kovacsics and Ye. As our main result, we show that separably closed non-trivially valued fields of arbitrary imperfection degree admit beautiful pairs which are elementary pairs satisfying certain natural axioms. They satisfy beauty transfer, i.e., saturated models of their theory are again beautiful. The same holds for beautiful pairs associated to natural subclasses of all definable types, most notably for all definable types orthogonal to the value group and for all bounded definable types. This yields strict pro-definability of the space of the definable types from any of these classes, in the theory SCVF of separably closed non-trivially valued fields. We also show a separable analog of a classical result of Keisler's, namely that the first order theory of an infinite separable extension $L/K$ of fields - considered in the pairs language and where the large field $L$ is separably closed, is determined by the theory of the small field $K$ together with the imperfection degree of $L$ over $K$.
item.dc:creator: Zhengqing He, Martin Hils

item.title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.15785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open. In this paper, we analyze the structure of tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets: bounded open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ whose boundary is a finite union of line segments parallel to the axes. We prove that every such tiling that is topologically minimal is weakly periodic. Moreover, we show that if an axis-parallel polygonal set $\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^2$ then it admits a quasi-periodic tiling (i.e., a finite union of translated lattices). The proofs combine geometric decompositions of tilings with rational approximation and discrete tiling theory. As a consequence, we obtain that the translational tiling problem for axis-parallel polygonal sets with real algebraic vertex coordinates is decidable.
item.dc:creator: Jaume de Dios Pont, Jan Greb\'ik, Rachel Greenfeld, Jos\'e Madrid

item.title: Some complete $\omega$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2610.16473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fix a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $\Sigma^\omega$ in $\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k$, and by $\checked{D}_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $\Sigma$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $\omega$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:=\{ w_0w_1\cdots\in\Sigma^\omega\mid\forall i\in\omega ~~w_i\in U_{n,k}\}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $\checked{D}\_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0\_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k>3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbf{\Delta}^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].
item.dc:creator: Jacques Duparc (UNIL), Olivier Finkel (IMJ-PRG), Dominique Lecomte (IMJ-PRG)

item.title: Model theory of quasitracial $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras and the absoluteness of monotone completeness
item.description: arXiv:2610.17435v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine various applications of logic to $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras, particularly the monotone completeness conjecture. We develop a model theory for $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras equipped with a faithful normalized quasitrace. Using this language, we provide a separable coding which allows us to reduce the finite case of the monotone completeness conjecture to monotone sequential completeness of $\mathrm{II}_1$ $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factors. Combining an explicit recursive axiomatization with the completeness theorem for continuous logic, we show that this case of the conjecture, and Kaplansky's problem whether every $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factor of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ is a von Neumann algebra, are each equivalent in ZFC to a $\Pi^0_2$ sentence of arithmetic, so that their answers are the same in every $\omega$-model of ZFC. We also consider real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras. Here the Baer-$*$-ring notion of an abelian projection must be distinguished from commutativity; following the real-operator-algebra terminology we call the former semi-abelian. Handelman's matrix theorem implies that a real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebra with no nonzero central semi-abelian projection has $\mathrm{AW}^*$ complexification. We answer a number of other open problems in real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Jananan Arulseelan

item.title: Finite-on-Top-of-Temporal CSPs in Fixed-Point Logic
item.description: arXiv:2610.18287v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study definability in fixed-point logic with counting (FPC) for a class of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) that simultaneously generalises finite-domain CSPs and temporal CSPs. The templates for the CSPs are first-order expansions of the structure $([k] \times {\mathbb Q};<_1,\dots,<_k,\sim)$ where $<_i \, := \{((i,x),(i,x')) \mid x<x'\}$ and $\sim \, := \{((i,x),(i,x')) \mid i \in [k], x,x' \in {\mathbb Q}\}$, i.e., $k$ copies of $({\mathbb Q};<)$. Such a CSP is definable in FPC precisely when the template pp-constructs neither the ternary temporal relation $X$, which holds on three elements if the minimum is attained exactly twice, nor a nontrivial finite affine structure. Equivalently, the template has global polymorphisms that witness the tractability of the temporal CSPs on the copies, and that provide 3-4 weak near-unanimity operations on the set of copies of ${\mathbb Q}$. In this case, we prove that the CSP is even expressible in the less expressive logic FP$^*$, which is the restriction of FPC without counting terms (i.e., the extension of first-order logic by a fixed point operator and an ordered auxiliary number sort). Our algorithm samples finitely many values in each copy and then performs nested constraint-singleton consistency tests (which is a uniform polynomial-time algorithm for finite-domain CSPs). The correctness proof uses finite-domain CSP theory to combine consistency certificates by a single polymorphism term, fixing each variable to one copy without destroying the certificates needed for the temporal algorithm. We then use a known normal form for algebraic products to control the remaining interactions between different copies.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Bodirsky, Philipp A. Grzywaczyk

item.title: Ramsey properties of trees and $C$-relations via the partite construction
item.description: arXiv:2610.18402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finite convexly ordered binary branching $C$-relations have been viewed as a notable exception to the broad applicability of the partite construction in structural Ramsey theory. The absence of a proof of their Ramsey property by the partite construction was noted by Bodirsky in his 2015 survey and pointed out again by Hubi\v{c}ka and Kone\v{c}n\'y in their 2026 survey. We overcome this limitation by giving proofs based on the partite construction of the known Ramsey properties of the class $\mathcal{CT}$ of finite convexly ordered treeable meet semilattices and of the classes of finite convexly ordered $C$-relations with arbitrary branching and with binary branching. Our proofs do not rely on Milliken's tree theorem. The key is to expand $\mathcal{CT}$ by level predicates and a predecessor function so that the locally finite subclass method applies. We then transfer the resulting Ramsey witnesses to the corresponding reduct classes and to the classes of convexly ordered $C$-relations.
item.dc:creator: Hyoyoon Lee

item.title: High-Arity Rademacher Complexity and Uniform Laws of Large Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.18528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize several properties of higher-arity function classes, specifically finite $\VC_k$-dimension, slicewise finite $\VC$-dimension, and finite slicewise Littlestone dimension, in terms of generalizations of Rademacher complexity. These characterizations sets up simple new proofs of several results on finite $\VC_k$-dimension and slicewise finite $\VC$-dimension. These include the preservation of finite $\VC_k$-dimension under taking expectations and uniform law of large numbers statements for both properties. All of these results apply naturally to real-valued function classes as well as boolean-valued classes. We also prove a new adversarial uniform law of large numbers for classes with finite slicewise Littlestone dimension.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Anderson, Henry Towsner

item.title: Chain Continuity and Scott-Closed Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.18692v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every chain-continuous dcpo is continuous and that its way-below relation is the relational square of its chain-below relation, answering a question of Ern\'e. A subalgebra lattice obtained from a locally finite J\'onsson algebra shows that the chain-below relation itself need not interpolate. For approximation by Scott-closed sets, we give a finite-upper-bound characterization on lower-set lattices and characterize interpolation by an extension property for directed lower sets. This yields a countably based, completely distributive algebraic lattice on which chain and directed approximation coincide, whereas Scott-closed approximation fails to interpolate, answering questions of Ern\'e and of Ho and Zhao.
item.dc:creator: Yuxu Chen

item.title: Separation of congruence intervals and implications
item.description: arXiv:2007.07237v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Constraint Satisfaction Problem (CSP) has been intensively studied in many areas of computer science and mathematics. The approach to the CSP based on tools from universal algebra turned out to be the most successful one to study the complexity and algorithms for this problem. Several techniques have been developed over two decades. One of them is through associating edge-colored graphs with algebras and studying how the properties of algebras are related with the structure of the associated graphs. This approach has been introduced in our previous two papers (A.Bulatov, Local structure of idempotent algebras I,II. arXiv:2006.09599, arXiv:2006.10239, 2020). In this paper we further advance it by introducing new structural properties of finite idempotent algebras omitting type 1 such as separation congruences, collapsing polynomials, and their implications for the structure of subdirect products of finite algebras. This paper also provides the algebraic background for our proof of Feder-Vardi Dichotomy Conjecture (A. Bulatov, A Dichotomy Theorem for Nonuniform CSPs. FOCS 2017: 319-330).
item.dc:creator: Andrei A. Bulatov

item.title: MS-measurability via coordinatization
item.description: arXiv:2109.11760v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study $MS$-measurability of structures obtained as expansions of finite-height trees. We show that an admissible nil-interaction coordinatized structure is $MS$-measurable whenever its canonical component theories are $MS$-measurable and their universes have dimension one. The dimension of a complete type is the sum of its local component dimensions, and its measure is the product of the corresponding local measures. We also show that, in the countable $\aleph_0$-categorical setting, an admissible nil-interaction structure is interdefinable with its canonical tree product. These products preserve supersimplicity of finite $SU$-rank and one-basedness, with global $SU$-rank given by a sum of local ranks. Finite homogeneous component approximations give finite tree envelopes, yielding preservation of smooth approximability. Enriched finite tree products of multidimensional asymptotic classes, respectively exact classes, again form multidimensional asymptotic classes, respectively exact classes. For the corresponding reducts, the conclusion is weak unless the coordinate enrichment can be recovered uniformly.
item.dc:creator: Mostafa Mirabi

item.title: Convex Team Logics
item.description: arXiv:2503.21850v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove expressive completeness results for convex propositional and modal team logics, where a logic is convex if, for each formula, if it is true in two teams $t$ and $u$ and $t\subseteq s\subseteq u$, then it is also true in $s$. We introduce propositional/modal team logics which are expressively complete for the class of all convex propositional/modal team properties. We also answer an open question concerning the expressive power of classical propositional logic extended with the nonemptiness atom NE: we show that it is expressively complete for the class of all convex and union-closed properties. A modal analogue of this result additionally yields an expressive completeness theorem for Aloni's (2022) Bilateral State-Based Modal Logic. There is a specific sense in which one of the propositional convex logics we introduce extends propositional dependence logic; this sense corresponds to the existence of a compositional translation between the two logics. Another of the convex logics extends propositional inquisitive logic in the same manner. We generalize the notion of uniform definability, as considered in the team semantics literature, to formalize this notion of compositional extension.
item.dc:creator: Aleksi Anttila, S{\o}ren Brinck Knudstorp

item.title: A definable matching theorem and approximate Grothendieck semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2507.08463v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an arbitrary first-order structure, we introduce the notion of an approximate Grothendieck semigroup, which satisfies a Banach-Schr\"oder-Bernstein Theorem, as well as a weak Cancellation Law (wCL). At the heart of the proof of the wCL lies a definable matching theorem, which vastly generalizes a related result in Ma\v{r}\'{i}kov\'{a} \cite{mat}, and is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Jana Ma\v{r}\'ikov\'a

item.title: Supervaluation-Style Truth Revisited
item.description: arXiv:2510.01883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Supervaluational fixed-point semantics for truth cannot be axiomatized because of its recursion-theoretic complexity. Johannes Stern (\emph{Supervaluation-Style Truth Without Supervaluations}, Journal of Philosophical Logic, 2018) proposed a new strategy (supervaluational-style truth) to capture the essential aspects of the supervaluational evaluation schema whilst limiting its recursion-theoretic complexity, hence resulting in ($\nat$-categorical) axiomatizations. Unfortunately, as we show in the paper, this strategy was not fully realized in Stern's original work: in fact, we provide counterexamples to some of Stern's key claims. However, we also vindicate Stern's project by providing different semantic incarnations of the idea and corresponding $\nat$-categorical axiomatizations. The results provide a deeper picture of the relationships between standard supervaluationism and supervaluational-style truth.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Dopico, Carlo Nicolai, Johannes Stern

item.title: Asymptotic classes via definable quotients
item.description: arXiv:2608.03993v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study when uniform interpretations and definable quotients preserve finite-dimensional asymptotic classes. Counting in the ambient structures gives finitely many asymptotic alternatives. However, the corresponding parameter sets need not be definable in the interpreted language, so in general the interpreted class is only weakly asymptotic. We define trace reflection, a one-sided condition which ensures this definability. We first prove a transfer theorem for interpretations with definable selectors and give explicit bounds on the denominator. We then use invariant profiles to prove a transfer theorem for general definable quotients, without assuming definable choice. We define an intrinsic visible denominator and prove that it is the least asymptotic denominator. We also give a coprime-witness criterion for the interpretation-dependent bound to be sharp. We prove formula-wise, syntactic, and semantic criteria for descent, as well as composition theorems, and show that trace reflection is strictly weaker than uniform weak bi-interpretability. Using profiles of finite frames, we remove the noncanonical parameters used to reconstruct finite-field coordinates. As applications, we study projective quotient traces and show that, for every fixed $k\geq2$, the pure incidence structures given by graphs of polynomials of degree less than $k$ over finite fields form a full $k$-dimensional asymptotic class. The denominator $k$ is minimal, and every member is $K_{k,n}$-free for all $n\geq2$.
item.dc:creator: Mostafa Mirabi

item.title: Uniform generalization of Goodstein's theorem and Cichon's independence proof
item.description: arXiv:2609.24214v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We uniformly generalize Goodstein's theorem (Goodstein 1944) and Cichon's independence proof (Cichon 1983) via the concept of maximality quotients.
item.dc:creator: Gunnar Wilken

item.title: $n$-variable theorems for dividing lines characterized by positive consistency-inconsistency configurations, and their applications to preservation problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.36394v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a class of classes of complete first-order theories, denoted by $\mathfrak{D}_{n\text{-var}}$, using positive consistency-inconsistency configurations and generalized indiscernibles. It contains the classes of stable, simple, NIP, NTP$_1$, NTP$_2$, NATP, NCTP, NBTP, NWP, NGP, and NPM$^{(k)}$ theories. For any dividing line $D\in\mathfrak{D}_{n\text{-var}}$ and any complete first-order theory $T\notin D$, we can always find a formula $\varphi(x,y)$ witnessing $T\notin D$ with an indexed set of parameters such that the set of its instances required to be consistent has a realization whose algebraic dimension over the whole set of parameters is $|x|$. We call statements of this form $n$-variable theorems, as they may be regarded as weak versions of one-variable theorems. Under the appropriate hypotheses on $T$, we prove that $T\in D$ if and only if the corresponding theory belongs to $D$ for (i) $T^{gt}$, (ii) $T_P$, (iii) $T^{ind}$, (iv) $T^G_K$, (v) ACF$_T$, and (vi) any completion of $T^{\bar\delta,nc}_g$. These are, respectively, the theories of generic trivializations, lovely pair expansions, $H$-structure expansions, vector spaces with a dense-codense generic $K$-subspace, algebraically closed fields with a distinguished subfield, and generic non-commutative derivations of algebraically bounded fields. The $n$-variable theorem is essential in proving (i)--(v). We also prove preservation for a special case of Mordell-Lang theories. We extend the framework to a larger class $\mathfrak{D}^h_{n\text{-var}}\supseteq\mathfrak{D}_{n\text{-var}}$, capturing higher-arity dividing lines such as NOP$_k$, NFOP$_k$, and NIP$_k$ for $1<k<\omega$. The $n$-variable theorem and preservation results (ii), (iii), (iv), and (vi) also hold for this larger class, while (i) holds assuming ${\rm acl=dcl}$.
item.dc:creator: Joonhee Kim

item.title: Closure Semantics for Weak Modal Logics: Completeness and Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.01433v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weak modal logics can be obtained by restricting the axioms and inference rules governing the modal operator. At the extreme, one may consider the least modal logic, in which no specifically modal axiom or inference rule is imposed. We introduce closure semantics, a new possible-world semantics for such weak modal logics, and establish soundness and strong completeness for a range of systems. We also give truth-preserving translations between closure models and other possible-world semantics, including neighborhood, FMT, and Kripke semantics.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Nishimura

item.title: The Higher Closed Null Ideal(s)
item.description: arXiv:2610.05784v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We generalise the $\sigma$-ideal $\mathcal E$ generated by the closed Lebesgue null subsets of the Cantor space ${}^\omega 2$ to the context of higher Cantor spaces ${}^\kappa 2$ for an uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ satisfying $\kappa=\kappa^{<\kappa}$. We introduce candidates for a higher closed null ideal based on slaloms on partitions of $\kappa$ into sets of size ${<}\kappa$, and study their combinatorial properties. We also give some relations between the cardinal characteristics of the higher closed null ideals and other cardinal characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Adam Marton, Jaroslav \v{S}upina, Miroslav Repick\'y, Tristan van der Vlugt

item.title: G\"odel Implication on Finite Chains: Catalan Enumeration and a Continuum Limit Law
item.description: arXiv:2602.16135v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the distribution of output values produced by all fully bracketed implication terms on $n$ distinct variables in G\"odel $m$-valued logic on the finite chain $V_m$. The Catalan decomposition of bracketings yields a stratified system of recurrences for the output counts. Passing to tail sums reduces this system to a finite iteration of a single map $\Phi_x$ and its inverse branch $\Psi_x$. For each fixed $m$, this reduction gives a common dominant square-root singularity at $r=1/(4m)$, coefficient asymptotics of order $(4m)^n n^{-3/2}$, and limiting proportions for every truth level. In the four-valued case these proportions are obtained explicitly in nested radicals. The main new phenomenon appears when the number of truth values also tends to infinity. If $K_m$ denotes the output level under the limiting $n\to\infty$ distribution and $X_m=K_m/(m-1)$, then $X_m\Rightarrow X$, where $X$ has density $(1+2t)^{-3/2}$ on $[0,1)$ together with an atom of mass $1/\sqrt{3}$ at $1$. In particular, the top mass converges to $1/\sqrt{3}$, while the bottom mass is asymptotic to $1/m$. We further show that the same probability law arises intrinsically when G\"odel implication is defined directly on $[0,1]$ and valuations are sampled from Lebesgue product measure: the continuum tail generating function satisfies an exact first-order differential equation whose critical specialization is the ODE appearing in the finite-chain Euler limit. We also record a root-split refinement whose pair-count generating functions factor as products of the level generating functions and inherit the same square-root scale.
item.dc:creator: Volkan Yildiz

item.title: Failure of the strong feasible disjunction property
item.description: arXiv:2604.04830v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A propositional proof system $P$ has the strong feasible disjunction property iff there is a constant $c \geq 1$ such that whenever $P$ admits a size $s$ proof of $\bigvee_i \alpha_i$ with no two $\alpha_i$ sharing an atom then one of $\alpha_i$ has a $P$-proof of size $\le s^c$. We combine the work of Ilango (2025) and Ren et al. (2025) with the gadget proof complexity generator of K. (2007) and rule out the property for strong enough proof systems under the following two hypotheses: - there exists a language in class E that requires exponential size circuits even if they are allowed to query an NP oracle, - there exists a P/poly demi-bit in the sense of Rudich (1997).
item.dc:creator: Jan Krajicek

item.title: Optimizing Proof-Search via Linearization for G\"odel-L\"ob Logic with Tree-Hypersequents
item.description: arXiv:2606.03484v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We answer a question posed by Poggiolesi concerning a syntactic decidability proof for GL in the tree-hypersequent system CSGL, and resolve a challenge identified by Maggesi and Perini Brogi, who sought a PSPACE proof-search algorithm for GL in expressive sequent-based formalisms. We work with a notational variant of CSGL formulated in terms of (labeled) tree sequents. Our answer is complexity-optimal: we present a proof-search algorithm that decides the (in)validity of formulae and runs in PSPACE, matching the known PSPACE-completeness of GL. To achieve this, we introduce a "linearization method", which constructs only a single branch of a derivation and of a tree sequent at a time, avoiding the exponential blowup typical of naive proof-search in sequent formalisms. We show how to systematically combine fragments of tree sequents generated during proof-search to extract finite counter-models, which serves as a theoretical device for establishing the correctness of the algorithm when proof-search fails. Finally, we show that every valid formula admits a proof consisting solely of line sequents, which correspond to linear nested sequents. This establishes a connection between depth-first proof-search and linear nested sequent calculi. Our results not only answer the aforementioned questions, but also provide new insights into proof-search and correctness arguments in tree sequent systems for modal logics.
item.dc:creator: Tim S. Lyon (TU Dresden, Germany), Omar Y. A. A. Taher (TU Dresden, Germany)

item.title: Beth companions of finitary essentially algebraic theories
item.description: arXiv:2609.03601v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For categories, being balanced (meaning that every arrow that is both epic and monic is an isomorphism) can be regarded as a strong tameness property which plays an important role, for example, in algebra and logic. We study the problem of associating a balanced companion category, called a \emph{Beth companion}, to a locally finitely presentable category (equivalently, the category of models of a finitary essentially algebraic theory). We show that, if it exists, the Beth companion is unique and can be described in terms of \emph{saturated} objects. Under additional assumptions, we prove that Beth companions can be computed as orthogonality classes, and admit a syntactic presentation via Gabriel--Ulmer duality. Furthermore, we establish conditions for the transfer of properties from a category to its Beth companion. A number of examples of categories that do or do not admit a Beth companion are provided. In particular, we show that the category of commutative rings does not admit a Beth companion, and employ Pierce sheaf representations to describe the Beth companion of other classes of rings.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Di Liberti, Luca Reggio

item.title: Robust order properties in the HLM construction
item.description: arXiv:2609.19015v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Green's arithmetic regularity lemma over $G=\F_2^n$ has tower-type lower bounds. We show that the large order properties in the Hosseini--Lovett--Moshkovitz--Shapira (HLM) construction survive sparse edits. If $d$ is the top block dimension, then changing at most $|G|/16$ points of the top HLM set $A_s$ still leaves a half-graph of height $d/8$. For a suitable choice of the HLM maps, changing at most $\eps|G|$ points of a superlevel set of the averaged witness still leaves a half-graph of height $d/(8\sqrt{s})\ge{\rm twr}(s-2)$. The proofs use Sauer's lemma and the binary code formed by the top-level row traces.
item.dc:creator: Dean Matthew Menezes

item.title: Proofs Without Nominals: G\"odel's Ontological Argument, its Shallow Embedding, and the Open Questions of the Monatshefte Notes
item.description: arXiv:2609.36279v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The shallow embedding of higher-order modal logic in classical higher-order logic, used in Benzm\"uller and Scott's Notes on G\"odel's and Scott's variants of the ontological argument, reaches beyond the modal object language: its property quantifiers range over domains containing the nominals and satisfaction operators of hybrid logic. A proof using one proves a theorem of the embedding, not necessarily of the modal logic. That the framework affords this is not new. Whether a result is one of the modal logic can be settled by replaying it in an explicit calculus, one result at a time. More cheaply, and for all results at once, it can be approached by analysing what the embedding's proofs substitute. Every statement the Notes prove has a proof in the embedding substituting nothing outside the object language: 294 of them explicit proofs, machine-checked, none using a nominal. The Notes' own proofs substitute none either; what the check flags are terms a prover introduced. The three questions the Notes leave open are settled too, without nominals, but by the empty instance of the conjunction axiom, too cheaply to convince. As the Notes generalise it, to cover G\"odel's "any number of summands", the axiom covers the empty conjunction and the singleton. This article restricts it to at least two different conjuncts, a non-degenerate reading of G\"odel's footnote, and settles the questions again, without nominals. In effect the restriction excludes only the empty conjunction; the one-element case comes back with the other axioms. In one of the three variants the restriction refutes the possible existence of a God-like being; the answers return, with no side condition, once the Notes' non-emptiness clause is confined to G\"odel's essence. Every theorem stated here is verified in Isabelle/HOL and independently in Lean 4; the countermodels are Nitpick's, checked by the build.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Benzm\"uller
